text_blocks.snippet: The most common symptom of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is shortness of breath that starts during physical activity and eventually happens at rest.

PAH is high blood pressure in the arteries of your lungs. In the early stages, you might not notice any signs at all. As the condition progresses and puts strain on the heart, symptoms become more noticeable.

list.snippet: Shortness of breath during daily tasks like climbing stairs or exercising.
Fatigue and a general lack of energy.
Swelling (edema) in the feet, ankles, legs, and later the belly or neck due to fluid build-up.
Dizziness or fainting spells, especially during physical exertion.
Heart palpitations or a racing, pounding heartbeat.
Bluish lips or fingers (cyanosis) caused by lower oxygen levels.

text_blocks.snippet: You can learn more about these signs through the American Lung Association.
